subject: Discovery recap: Finly latency & concurrency targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Finly latency & concurrency targets

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have aligned next steps. Let me know if I missed anything.

Attendees:
- Alex Johnson (Finly)
- Priya Kumar (Finly)
- Marissa Cole (Redwood)
- Aditya Rao (Redwood)
- Rishi Malhotra (Redwood)

Top pain points you shared:
- Streaming UX feels choppy for advisors: token-by-token latency spikes cause partial sentences and UX flicker.
- Tail latency (p95) for interactive streaming is inconsistent and occasionally >600ms, which hurts adoption.
- Throughput / concurrency: current service degrades above ~120 simultaneous streaming sessions; need stable support for ~200 concurrent sessions and bursts to ~500.
- Cost: current architecture is expensive per session and prevents large-scale rollout.

Current stack summary (what you told us):
- In-house API that proxies to hosted model endpoints; no persistent KV cache, limited batching, ad-hoc horizontal scaling.
- Models: mix of open LLMs hosted on cloud endpoints (latency varies by region).
- Observability: basic request logs and sampling; no systematic tail-latency dashboards.

Success criteria for a pilot / evaluation:
- p95 interactive streaming latency (end-to-end visible tokens) <= 350ms under steady state.
- Support 200 concurrent streaming sessions with 2-3 tokens/sec per session, and graceful burst handling to 500 sessions.
- Streaming UX: smooth first-byte + low token-to-token jitter (measure via synthetic sessions).
- Cost: per-session unit cost improvement versus current baseline (we'll measure once you share baseline metrics).

Proposed next steps / owners:
- Marissa / Aditya: share a short test plan and what traffic/sample payloads look like (attached: finly_latency_test_plan.xlsx).
- Alex / Priya: share production traffic sample logs + baseline p95 numbers and target SLOs (we can accept anonymized logs).
- Redwood (Aditya / Rishi): provision sandbox with dedicated pool for a 3-day performance run; provide a short demo of streaming behavior and kernel/quantization plan.
- Schedule: propose technical demo + sandbox access early next week (Tues/Wed).

Attachments:
- finly_latency_test_plan.xlsx (test vectors, scenario descriptions)

If this matches what you captured, I'll send calendar invites for the demo and start the sandbox provisioning.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

---

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Kumar <pri.kumar@finly.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly latency & concurrency targets

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and captures the discussion. A few clarifications from our side:

- p95 target: we are aiming for p95 <= 400ms for visible streaming tokens to be conservative (our product team thinks 350ms is ideal but 400ms is an acceptable target for the pilot).
- Concurrency: 200 steady-state is accurate. Bursts to 500 are occasional (peak minutes), but we do need graceful degradation (no timeouts).
- Traffic profile: ~60% of sessions are short (20-30 tokens), 40% have longer interactive flows (200+ tokens).

We will:
- Share anonymized request logs (headers + timestamps + relative token counts) by EOD Monday.
- Confirm which Finly engineers will join the demo (likely Priya + our infra lead).

Questions for Redwood: can you confirm whether the sandbox will expose streaming token-by-token metrics (token latencies) and whether you'll enable prefix KV caching for the pilot? Also can you include a quantized model variant option to test cost/latency tradeoffs?

Appreciate it — looking forward to the demo.

Best,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Senior Product Manager | Finly
alex.johnson@finly.com

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>, Priya Kumar <pri.kumar@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly latency & concurrency targets

Great — thanks for the clarifications, Alex. Quick answers to your questions and next steps: 

- Sandbox capabilities: yes, the sandbox will stream token-by-token and we will surface per-token latency metrics as well as aggregated p50/p95/p99 dashboards during the run. We'll also provide raw traces for a subset of sessions for debugging.
- KV caching: we can enable prefix/KV caching for the pilot; we'll document configuration and expected hit-rate tradeoffs in the test plan.
- Quantized variant: we will include a 4-bit quantized model variant for comparison (latency vs. quality/cost).

I've booked a 60-minute technical demo + kickoff on Tuesday 2026-02-24 at 10:00 AM PT — invite sent to the attendees you mentioned. Link: https://meet.redwood.ai/finly-demo.

Next immediate items (owners):
- Alex / Priya (Finly): share logs and confirm demo attendees by Mon COB.
- Marissa (Redwood): share sandbox access + credentials and interim perf report after the first 24 hours.
- Aditya / Rishi (Redwood): prepare the quantized variant and KV cache config for the pilot.

Attachments: redwood_p95_report.pdf (sample p95 analysis from a comparable customer).

If that works, we'll move forward with sandbox provisioning Monday morning.

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
